why: B is false (not_B): it allows n = 1 (the circle), where clause (d) ('best possible': a geodesic of length πR whose end points are conjugate) fails — S¹ has no conjugate points. Counter-model: S¹ ⊆ ℝ², ψ = inclusion (IsRoundSphereR 1), induced connection. Hence ¬(A → B) and B ⇒ A only ex falso. Corrected Bcorr (n ≥ 2), for abstract M isometric via ψ to the radius-R sphere: (a) sectional curvature 1/R², (b) K(U,U) = (n−1)/R² for unit U, (c) every geodesic of length > πR has a conjugate pair, (d) a geodesic of length πR with conjugate end points, (e) for every ℓ < πR a geodesic of length ℓ without conjugate pairs. A (unit sphere Sⁿ ⊆ ℝⁿ⁺¹ only): K(U,U) = (n−1)‖U‖² for all U, the Myers hypothesis with r = 1, and for n ≥ 2 Myers (γ(0) conjugate to an interior γ(t), not minimal) plus diameter ≤ π. On the embedded unit sphere A ⇒ (b), (c) (proved); (a), (d) hold by project lemmas OUTSIDE A (curvOp_sph, conjMultiplicity_greatCircle; proved); (e), radius R ≠ 1 and abstract M via ψ are not covered. A has the diameter bound, non-minimality and the non-unit Ricci formula, absent from B.
